A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T1 framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original arithmetic-verification experiments, MATH500, GSM8K, and MMLU-Pro evaluations, and additional diagnostic experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds comparisons, component ablations, and computational-cost analyses.

M1.justification: The tool-based filtering stage, subsequent reward-model scoring, distillation objectives, and task-specific procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B. Renaming self-verification to verification and evaluating additional control methods do not change the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic arithmetic, MATH500, GSM8K, and the Health, Economics, and History domains of MMLU-Pro. The MMLU-Pro experiments move to Appendix E.1 in v2; they are not removed. No new dataset or task coverage is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 substantially extends comparisons beyond majority voting and conventional GenRM/PRM baselines. Figure 9 evaluates a distilled 1B adaptation of the tool-integrated Themis method, while Tables 5–7 add two-stage GenRM without tools and ToolV-only comparisons. These directly test competing explanations for T1's advantages.

E3.justification: V2 introduces compute-budget comparisons using token-based rescaling: 1.14 times for GenRM and approximately twice the budget for PRM. It also adds stage-isolation controls and a 3B arithmetic-verification configuration. These extend the evaluation design; the retained experiments' splits, training hyperparameters, sampling temperatures, and 64-solution protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether both verification stages are needed, whether an additional GenRM stage can replace tool integration, and whether benefits survive accounting for computational overhead (Section 6.4 and Appendices E.5–E.7). Existing difficulty, category, model-size, data-efficiency, confusion-matrix, and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, actual random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 promises a future package containing seeds, but does not supply new statistical reporting for the results.

E6.justification: V2 adds 3B arithmetic and Themis results, token-cost measurements, budget-dependent findings, and component-control scores. At N=64, Table 5 reports 46.0% for two-stage GenRM versus 45.4% for one-stage GenRM and 50.6% with ToolV. Table 6 adds ToolV-only accuracy of 52.4% versus 53.2% with PRM. Original benchmark plots and diagnostic scores are retained; Tables 8–16 redisplay existing plotted results.

T1.justification: Lemma 5.1, Theorems 5.2–5.3, their assumptions, and their appendix proofs retain the same mathematical substance. Relabeling Theorem C.1 as Lemma C.1 is editorial. The new discussion of idealized theory in Appendix C.1 qualifies interpretation without changing the formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list shift emphasis from self-verification and cross-domain generalization toward candidate verification, the two-stage design, and mathematical benchmarks. The central claims about tool-assisted small-model verification and the 1B-versus-8B comparison remain. Knowledge-intensive applicability is still claimed in the conclusion and supported in the appendix.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly describes the theory as an idealized conceptual illustration, explains the complementary execution and reasoning signals of the two stages, and discusses memory and compute tradeoffs. It newly acknowledges that PRM alone can perform better at small budgets. Existing false-negative and parallel-scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 describes GPT-4o trajectory distillation for the Themis adaptation and reports token usage by stage. Its new reproducibility statement promises scripts, prompts, configurations, instructions, and seeds, but supplies no package link. Existing Appendix D hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, and evaluation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to CRITIC, PAD, and Singhi et al. (2025). It also develops the distinction between T1's two-stage small-model verification and Themis's unified tool-augmented reward modeling; Li et al. (2024) was already cited in v1. The broader related-work organization remains.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title, abstract, introductory framing, and contribution bullets, and replaces much self-verification terminology. It moves the MMLU-Pro discussion into Appendix E, reorganizes appendix subsections, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements. Most method, theory, and existing experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts conference typography and layout, redraws Figure 1, and adds Themis and compute-budget plots. It adds cost and ablation tables plus nine tables giving exact values for existing benchmark plots. MMLU-Pro figures move into the appendix, and several retained displays are repositioned and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's support for the central design: comparison with a tool-integrated competitor, isolation of each stage's contribution, and assessment of additional computation. Figure 9, Figures 10–11, and Tables 5–7 substantially strengthen that evidence. The explicit small-budget tradeoff and qualification of the theory also improve interpretation. Compute accounting remains approximate and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
